With Sentry Mode on, only the USB-A port (where Sentry Mode saves its recordings) stays powered after you leave the car, so recording can continue. If the storage location is a drive on the Type-C port, that port loses power and recording switches to the drive on the USB-A port.

Writes to internal storage first, then moves each finished clip to the USB drive, reducing dropped frames on a slow drive. When on, recording doesn\'t switch to another USB drive if this one disconnects.

When over the cap or low on space, the oldest recordings are cleaned up automatically. Only unlocked files recorded by this app are deleted. Leave blank or enter 0 for no limit: nothing is deleted, and recording stops when space runs low.

Experimental, unofficial software with no vehicle safety certification. It does not replace the factory dashcam, reversing camera or blind-spot monitor. Do not use it while driving, and do not rely on its picture to judge the road.

Videos and photos go to a USB drive only; without one, recording doesn\'t start and no photos can be taken. Continuous writing would wear out the head unit\'s internal storage, which usually can\'t be replaced. Videos and photos aren\'t encrypted: anyone with the drive can read them.
